Carmine has a credit card which has no interest-free period. Interest is charged at 19.5% per annum, compounding daily, on the amount owing.

At the start of the month Carmine had an opening balance of \$162, and during the month Carmine used his credit card to purchase a phone for \$700.

He was charged interest on the opening balance for 30 days and on the purchase of the phone for 24 days.

How much interest was Carmine charged for the month?
questions.answer:
Daily rate $= \dfrac{0.195}{365}$.
$$I = 162\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{30} - 1\right] + 700\left[\left(1 + \tfrac{0.195}{365}\right)^{24} - 1\right] \approx 2.62 + 9.03 = \$11.65. \quad \textbf{(A)}$$

questions.question:
A ball is shot vertically into the air from the ground. The height of the ball above the ground, $h$ metres, can be modelled using the function $h = 20t - 5t^2$, where $t$ is measured in seconds. The graph of the height of the ball during its flight time is shown below.

For how many seconds is the height of the ball at least half its maximum height?
questions.answer:
The maximum is at $t = 2$ (the axis of symmetry, halfway between the zeros $t = 0$ and $t = 4$): $h = 40 - 20 = 20$ m.

Half the maximum is 10 m: $20t - 5t^2 = 10 \Rightarrow t^2 - 4t + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 2 \pm \sqrt2$.

Time at or above 10 m $= (2 + \sqrt2) - (2 - \sqrt2) = 2\sqrt2 \approx 2.8$ s. **(C)**

questions.question:
Box A contains 3 red balls and 2 white balls while box B contains 6 red balls and 1 white ball.

John draws a ball randomly from box A and then puts it into box B. If John draws a ball randomly from box B afterwards, what is the probability that John draws a red ball?
questions.answer:
Box B then holds 8 balls.
- Red moved ($\frac35$): B has 7 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac78$.
- White moved ($\frac25$): B has 6 red, $P(\text{red}) = \frac68$.

$$P(\text{red}) = \frac35 \times \frac78 + \frac25 \times \frac68 = \frac{21}{40} + \frac{12}{40} = \frac{33}{40}. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

Tree diagram ($W$ = Amanda wins, $\overline{W}$ = does not win):

- After $W$: $P(W) = \frac{4}{199}$, $P(\overline{W}) = \frac{195}{199}$

The diagram below shows the location of three cities and the airline routes connecting them.

City $H$ is 860 km from city $G$ on a bearing of $110^\circ$. City $F$ is 730 km due south of city $G$.

Find the distance, correct to the nearest km, and the bearing, correct to the nearest degree, of city $F$ from city $H$.
questions.answer:
$\angle FGH = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.

**Distance** (cosine rule):
$$FH^2 = 860^2 + 730^2 - 2(860)(730)\cos 70^\circ \approx 843\,059 \Rightarrow FH \approx 918\text{ km}$$

**Angle at $H$** (sine rule):
$$\frac{\sin \angle GHF}{730} = \frac{\sin 70^\circ}{918.18} \Rightarrow \angle GHF \approx 48.3^\circ$$

**Bearing:** the bearing of $G$ from $H$ is $110^\circ + 180^\circ = 290^\circ$. $F$ is $48.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from that direction:
$$290^\circ - 48.3^\circ \approx 242^\circ$$

$F$ is about **918 km from $H$ on a bearing of $242^\circ$**.

$$260^\circ + 143^\circ 22' - 360^\circ = 43^\circ 22'.$$
The bearing of $Q$ from $R$ is about **043°T**.

Take the cut through $B \to C$ (140), $D \to C$ (50) and $E \to F$ (120). Every path from $A$ to $G$ crosses it, and its capacity is

| Years | 2% | 4% | 6% | 8% | 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 57.0524 | 54.2991 | 51.7256 | 49.3184 | 47.0654 |

| 15 | 155.3981 | 135.1921 | 118.5035 | 104.6406 | 93.0574 |

| 25 | 235.9301 | 189.4525 | 155.2069 | 129.5645 | 110.0472 |

questions.answer:
Loan $= 1\,000\,000 - 60\,000 = \$940\,000$.

- Years 11–30 at \$7000: $7000 \times (166.7916 - 90.0735) = \$537\,026.70$

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

Farmer Tran wants to fence around the area $ABOD$. Find the cost of this project if each metre of fencing costs \$22.
questions.answer:
$\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 310^\circ + 21^\circ = 71^\circ$ and $\angle AOD = 310^\circ - 256^\circ = 54^\circ$.
$$AB^2 = 85^2 + 64^2 - 2(85)(64)\cos 71^\circ \implies AB \approx 88.20 \text{ m}$$
$$AD^2 = 85^2 + 70^2 - 2(85)(70)\cos 54^\circ \implies AD \approx 71.63 \text{ m}$$
Perimeter of $ABOD = 88.20 + 64 + 70 + 71.63 \approx 293.82$ m. Cost $\approx 293.82 \times 22 = \$6464.13$.

A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

The surveyor finds that the area of triangle $BOC$ is $1664\ \text{m}^2$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $O$.
questions.answer:
$\frac12 \times 64 \times 52 \times \sin\angle BOC = 1664 \implies \sin\angle BOC = 1 \implies \angle BOC = 90^\circ$.

Bearing of $C$ from $O$ $= 21^\circ + 90^\circ = 111^\circ$T.

By forward scanning, find the earliest start time of activity $K$.

ESTs: $C$: 3; $D$, $E$: $\max(6, 3 + 2) = 6$; $J$: $6 + 5 = 11$; $F$: 3.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

The project currently takes 19 weeks. The contractor proposes a reduction in completion time for activities $A$, $E$, $F$ and $L$, at an additional cost. The table below summarises these costs. Each activity can only be reduced by a maximum of three weeks.

| Activity | Weekly cost (\$) |
|---|---|
| $A$ | 130 000 |
| $E$ | 110 000 |
| $F$ | 120 000 |
| $L$ | 100 000 |

If the overall completion time for the project can be reduced to 15 weeks, find the minimum cost of this change. Your answer should explain clearly why the minimum cost is achieved.
questions.answer:
Every path must end up at most 15 weeks. Let $a$, $e$, $l$ be the reductions of $A$, $E$, $L$ ($F$ is on no long path, so reducing it does not help).

| Path | Length | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| $A$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + l \ge 4$ |
| $A$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + e + l \ge 4$ |
| $B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $l \ge 3$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $e + l \ge 3$ |
| $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 17 | $a + e \ge 2$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 16 | $e \ge 1$ |

$B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ forces $l = 3$ (the maximum), so $a + l \ge 4$ forces $a \ge 1$; $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ forces $e \ge 1$. Taking $a = 1$, $e = 1$, $l = 3$ meets every condition:
$$\text{Minimum cost} = 130\,000 + 110\,000 + 3 \times 100\,000 = \$540\,000.$$

(The paper's sample answer gives \$430 000 by reducing only $A$ and $L$, but that leaves $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks and $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks, so the project would still take 16 weeks.)
